subject: Pricing/discount follow-up — startup & committed-use options
messages:
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia@novaflow.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Martinez <carlos@novaflow.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + runbook discussion

Hi Ben / Marissa —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifications to help you size a proposal: 

Summary of our needs:
- Primary use: product chat + summarization for enterprise users (support + account management).
- Current baseline: ~3M tokens / month across two environments (staging + prod).
- Expected ramp: 3M -> 7–10M tokens/month over 6–9 months as we onboard more customers.
- Latency target: p95 < 400ms for short chat interactions.

Budget questions we have:
- Our rough budget is $80k–$140k ARR for inference today; open to committed-use if economics line up.
- Target unit economics: we were hoping to land around $50–$80 per 1M tokens once committed and on a startup program.

Ask: can Redwood outline a 12‑month startup discount + a committed-use sheet (1yr / 2yr) showing effective $/1M tokens at each tier? Also need procurement timeline — we’re aiming for a signed agreement by end of July.

Attachments: I’ve attached our internal traffic projection (summary) — let me know if you want the raw spreadsheet.

Best,
Sofia Ramos
Head of Product, NovaFlow
sofia@novaflow.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia@novaflow.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing/discount follow-up — startup & committed-use options

Sofia — thanks for the clear recap and the projection. Helpful. Quick follow-up items from my side so I can put together an accurate offer: 

1) Clarify volumes: when you say 7–10M in 6–9 months, is that a steady-state monthly target (e.g., after ramp you expect ~8M/mo ongoing), or a peak?
2) Is the $80k–$140k ARR budget flexible if the committed discount improves unit economics materially?
3) Any procurement requirements we should know about (POs, legal SOW, specific SOC2 evidence)?

High level on options we can draft: 
- Startup program: 12 months with an upfront credit and a % discount for first year (targeting 30–50% off list for early-stage customers).
- Committed-use: 12/24 month tiers with increasing discounts based on committed spend; we can show effective $/1M tokens for each tier.
- Multi‑year incentives: additional price protections and smaller incremental discounts (or billing smoothing) for 24+ month commitments.

If you confirm the ramp is steady-state and the budget band, I’ll draft two scenarios (startup 1yr + committed-use 1yr and 2yr) with the attached worksheet and a short term sheet for approvals. I’ll loop Marissa for pricing approvals and RevOps sign-off next week.

Proposed next step: I’ll send a draft offer by Friday (6/19). If that works, we can book a quick 30‑minute review to run numbers.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia@novaflow.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Martinez <carlos@novaflow.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing/discount follow-up — startup & committed-use options

Hi Ben —

Answers below: 
- Volume: the 7–10M is expected steady-state monthly after ramp (so think of it as the new baseline). Peak may hit ~12–14M for short periods, but baseline is what we care about for committed pricing.
- Budget flexibility: we can stretch to ~$200k ARR if committed pricing gets us under $60 / 1M tokens effective.
- Procurement: standard SaaS PO + our legal SOW; SOC2 Type II report and a standard security questionnaire will be required. Procurement timeline: aiming to complete legal and procurement by end of July.

A couple more context items:
- We’re an early-stage startup (Series A) and would prefer a startup program if the economics are reasonable.
- If committed-use delivers the right $/1M and a simple cancellation / downgrade path, we’d consider a 12–24 month commit.

Looking forward to the scenarios. Also please include any usage caps or overage terms in the sheet.

Thanks,
Sofia
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia@novaflow.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing/discount follow-up — startup & committed-use options

Sofia — apologies for the weekend send, wanted to get this in front of you before Monday. Attached are two items: Redwood-Startup-Offer-2026-06.pdf (short term sheet) and Committed-Use-Worksheet-2026-06.xlsx (breakdowns). Key highlights below — high level effective pricing rounded to nearest dollar: 

Scenario A — Startup program (12 months)
- Offer: 40% off list for first 12 months + $10k usage credit applied up front.
- Effective: given your current 3M/month -> annualized ~36M tokens first year. Estimated effective cost: $72 / 1M tokens (first year) after credit. If you ramp to 8M steady-state mid-year, first-year blended effective drops to ~$58 / 1M.

Scenario B — Committed-use 12 month (upfront commit)
- Tier 1: commit to $120k/year (baseline) -> ~25% discount -> effective ~$95 / 1M (at current volumes).
- Tier 2: commit to $240k/year -> ~40% discount -> effective ~$60 / 1M (at higher volumes).

Scenario C — Committed-use 24 month
- Additional 5–10% incentive on top of 12m committed discounts (e.g., 45% total at higher commit) + price protection. Effective ~$50–$55 / 1M at scale.

Notes / assumptions:
- These are illustrative based on the projection you shared; final numbers depend on exact monthly profile and whether discounts apply to list token rate vs. gross spend.
- Overages: billed at list rate after discounts (worksheet shows blended overage examples). We can add soft caps and alerts to avoid surprises.
- Security: SOC2 Type II available; Marissa will share the package and the CC lean on evidence.

Next steps: 
1) If any of the scenarios look good, sign the attached short term sheet (DocuSign link included in the PDF) and we’ll prepare a formal contract + RevOps billing schedule.
2) Marissa will validate the discount and formalize billing terms (billing frequency, PO flow).
3) We aim to get to a countersigned agreement by end of July to hit your timeline.

If helpful I can propose a quick call on Monday 6/22 to walk through the worksheet line by line.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: Redwood-Startup-Offer-2026-06.pdf (term sheet, 3 pages), Committed-Use-Worksheet-2026-06.xlsx (pricing model, 1 sheet)
